assessment.nobel_worthiness: Time-reversal-invariant topological insulators created a new classification of electronic phases in which band topology, spin-orbit coupling and symmetry protect boundary states. The Z2 insight and its first experimental realisation in HgTe wells reshaped how band structures are computed and searched, which is close to my own field of first-principles electronic structure. Originality and clarity are very high.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele supplied the theoretical framework (quantum spin Hall effect, Z2 invariant); Molenkamp's group delivered the first experimental demonstration in the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang-predicted HgTe system. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang and other early contributors are not in the credited names, so this triple is a defensible theory-plus-experiment configuration, though not the only possible one.
assessment.maturity: Fifteen to twenty years of independent confirmation, extension to three dimensions, many material realisations, ARPES and transport verification, and wide influence on photonic, magnetic and superconducting analogues. Recognition is timely and the interpretation is stable.
uncertainties: Credit for the 3D generalisation and for the first ARPES observations is not covered by the supplied names.
The supplied credit omits Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, and I cannot independently verify the relative priority claims.
Applications remain limited so far, though that is not a barrier for a discovery prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene opened moire flat-band physics, with correlated insulators and superconductivity in a tunable carbon-only system. The Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model made a quantitative prediction of flat bands at a magic angle, and the experiment realised it. This is a rare case where electronic-structure theory predicted a striking regime in advance.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the key theoretical prediction; Jarillo-Herrero's group performed the decisive experimental discovery of correlated states and superconductivity. Cao and others are not in the credited names, and the allocation among experimental co-authors is unresolved. The supplied triple is coherent.
assessment.maturity: Less than a decade old, but reproduced by many groups and generalised to other moire systems. Open questions remain on the pairing mechanism and on sample inhomogeneity, so some may regard it as slightly premature, but the core discovery is robust.
uncertainties: The mechanism of superconductivity is still debated.
Role of twist-angle disorder and strain in reported results is not fully settled.
Credit for the first experimental report beyond the named experimentalist is not resolved in the supplied text.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, using the magic-wavelength idea and reaching 10^-18 fractional uncertainty, are a transformative advance in precision measurement, with consequences for time standards, geodesy and fundamental-constant tests. Impact is lasting and the concept is clear and original.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and demonstrated the first lattice clocks; Ye led the push to extreme precision and stability. Two names give a clean, fair allocation, with possible contributions from others (for example Hall, Pritchard-era trapping groups, NIST ion-clock teams) outside the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent confirmation across several laboratories; redefinition of the second is under discussion. Mature enough, though the practical redefinition has not yet occurred.
uncertainties: Possible overlap with earlier-recognised frequency-comb and ion-clock work.
Whether further contributors deserve credit is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The experimental observation of the Higgs boson completed the Standard Model's electroweak sector and confirmed the 2013-recognised mechanism. The importance is beyond question, and the discovery is clear and cleanly confirmed.
assessment.attribution: The prize rules limit the award to three people while ATLAS and CMS each involved thousands. Della Negra, Jenni and Virdee are among the founding proponents of the detector concepts; Gianotti led ATLAS at the time of the announcement. Any selection is contested and I would choose the founding conception, acknowledging that Gianotti is an equally defensible choice.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature, independently confirmed by two experiments, with properties measured well. Recognition is timely, even somewhat overdue relative to the 2013 theory prize.
uncertainties: Attribution within very large collaborations is inherently arbitrary.
The statutes' three-person limit conflicts with the collective nature of the discovery.
The alternative candidate B029 covers machine and detector construction, creating overlap.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit quantum electrodynamics provides the architectural foundation for superconducting quantum processors and strong light-matter coupling on a chip. The impact on quantum technologies and fundamental tests is large, and the idea is clear and original.
assessment.attribution: Blais, Girvin and Schoelkopf (with Wallraff and Huard and others not in the names) developed the theory and first experiments; the supplied triple is reasonable but the experimental first demonstration is shared with others. Some overlap with the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits.
assessment.maturity: Twenty years of consolidation and broad independent adoption. Timing is good, though the committee may want distance from the 2025 award.
uncertainties: Overlap with the recent 2025 prize topic may reduce urgency.
Credit for the first strong-coupling experiment extends beyond the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum simulation with ultracold atoms in optical lattices realised Hubbard-type models with tunable parameters, giving access to many-body phases such as the Mott transition. For a theorist of correlated electrons this is a valuable analogue simulator, though its direct predictive power for real materials is still limited.
assessment.attribution: Zoller (with Jaksch, Cirac) provided the theoretical proposals; Bloch, Greiner and Esslinger carried out the decisive experiments. Five credited names exceed the three-laureate limit, so selection is difficult and Greiner and Cirac are left out with some unease.
assessment.maturity: Mature experimental platform with a large community; however the claim of solving open correlated-electron problems is not yet firmly established.
uncertainties: Uncertain whether the simulation has produced a decisive new physical discovery rather than a demonstration of capability.
Allocation among five credited names is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Femtosecond demagnetisation and all-optical switching opened ultrafast magnetism, and I know the field well from atomistic spin dynamics work. The original observation by Beaurepaire et al. was striking, and all-optical switching suggests routes to faster data storage. However, the microscopic mechanism of ultrafast demagnetisation remains debated, which weighs against the clarity criterion.
assessment.attribution: Beaurepaire made the original discovery of subpicosecond demagnetisation; Kimel and Rasing demonstrated optical control of magnetisation. Other groups (for example Stanciu et al., Ostler et al.) contributed to all-optical switching and are not credited. I note my own field proximity and treat that cautiously.
assessment.maturity: Two decades of work, widely reproduced; but the interpretation remains unsettled (spin-flip scattering versus superdiffusive transport versus others), so maturity is only moderate.
uncertainties: Microscopic mechanism still disputed.
Possible conflict of perspective given the proximity to my own research area.
Credit for all-optical switching is split among several groups.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Spin-orbit torques enable electrical switching of magnetisation without an external polarised current, with direct relevance for magnetic memory. The concept is important and has had a large technological pull.
assessment.attribution: Miron and Gambardella reported Rashba-torque switching; Buhrman reported spin-Hall-driven switching. The attribution between Rashba and spin Hall origins is partly unresolved and others (for example Ralph, Hirsch's spin Hall proposal) may merit consideration.
assessment.maturity: Reasonably mature and widely adopted in industry research, but origin of torques in various systems is still discussed and the field is evolving.
uncertainties: Competing explanations for torque origin in different materials.
Several plausible contributors lie outside the credited names.
